issues.problem: Local officials' alerts are ordered only by phase and send time. No line says how the message's area relates to the fire. On Eaton, the reference fire, the replay time shows 33 archived messages. The Official now row lists the 3 most recent first: an LA City warning for the Sunset Fire and two Runyon Canyon messages, 26-30 km from Eaton's reported location. Eaton's own LA County evacuation orders and warnings (8-20 km) are hidden behind '+30 more: see the Official filter'. No line gives a distance, says whether the area covers the fire, or says that the message does not say which fire it is about. The NWS fire weather rows do this ('covers the fire area' / 'zone N mi from the fire'). The location card at a point inside the fire's area at a past time has the same order. It also shows the fire's whole list, not filtered to the point. A new user can read another fire's 'Evacuate now' as Eaton's.
issues.evidence: docs/screenshots/review3-us-official-eaton-local-alerts-command-desktop.png. GET /api/official/local-alerts?incident=2025-eaton-fire-dbfa57&at_ms=1736394000000 on 8713 returns 33 alerts. The first 3 have nearest_km 29.5, 26.2 and 26.5 and covers_reported_location false. The LACo OEM / LACoFD orders and warnings have nearest_km 8.4-20.1. localAlerts.ts:164 sorts by ORDER[phase], then by sentMs descending. OfficialNow.tsx LocalAlertsRow and location/official.ts localAlertLines show slice(0, 3) without nearest_km or covers_reported_location. toLocalAlertItem drops nearest_km.
issues.fix: Keep nearest_km on LocalAlertItem. Order by relevance within a phase: covers_reported_location first, then nearest_km, then send time. On every line, in Official now, the card and the feed, add the same location phrase the NWS rows use: 'area covers the fire's reported location' or 'area N mi from the fire' (units from the user's setting). For 'polygon' matches that do not cover the location, add 'the message does not say which fire it is about'. Add a test with the recorded LA archive window: the nearest message comes first and every line has its location phrase.

issues.problem: notCheckedAt treats an unknown point state (geo lookup still loading) as checked whenever the NWS answer covers all 49 codes. So a point in Alaska, Canada or Mexico briefly reads 'Fire weather alerts (NWS): checked, none in effect here · Not an all-clear' until /api/geo/lookup answers, and only then 'not checked'.
issues.evidence: model.ts:646-648: `if (pointState === undefined) return coversLower48(d) ? null : {state:'loading'…}`. model.test.ts asserts this behaviour ('no lookup needed') for Reno, but it also applies to points outside the lower 48.
issues.fix: Return 'loading' while the state is unknown for a point that is not inside a lower-48 state. Use a cheap rule (the regions bbox of the lower 48), or always wait for the lookup, which is cached and fast. Add the Anchorage and Tijuana cases with pointState undefined.

issues.problem: CONTRACT §14.8.7 asks for the national NWS answer in the dev preset to have 'alerts in two zones', so that 'each alert in its own zone' can be seen. The recorded national fixture has 3 Red Flag Warnings, from NWS Billings MT, Riverton WY and Rapid City SD, all in America/Denver. The preset shows only MDT. The deviation is not listed in the report.
issues.evidence: docs/screenshots/review3-us-official-dev-preset-desktop.png: all three alerts are in MDT. web/src/official/__fixtures__/national.ts.
issues.fix: Add one recorded alert from another zone to the preset's national answer (for example a Pacific or Central office from the backend's recorded samples, parsed offline), or record the deviation in the report and the as-built note.

issues.problem: The credits list (useExtrasCredits, shown in the map attribution) has no line for local officials' alerts. There is no 'National Weather Service (relayed local officials' messages)' line, and no 'FEMA IPAWS archive via OpenFEMA' line with the notice, even when archived FEMA messages are on screen. The credit and the OpenFEMA notice appear only inline, on each archived line and under 'More'. The LIVE_CREDIT / ARCHIVE_CREDIT values that localAlertsState computes (`credits`) are never read.
issues.evidence: Eaton Command screenshot: the attribution bar names the NWS fire weather source (IEM archive) but not FEMA/OpenFEMA, while the Official now row shows FEMA archive messages. Grep: no use of LocalAlertsOfficial.credits outside localAlerts.ts.
issues.fix: Add a localAlertCredits(local) producer to useExtrasCredits. It names the live credit, and when the archive answered it also names the archive credit with the OpenFEMA notice (no FEMA logo). Add a unit test.

issues.problem: Cameras answer state_not_available outside California, but the answer's sources[] still lists the three California camera sources (Cal OES webcams, ALERTCalifornia, Caltrans). The camera panel then shows 'CalOES California Webcams · Cal OES · Public' as a source line under a Montana fire. This conflicts with the report's statement that no Cal OES text is shown for a non-California answer. The not-available sentence already names the California networks.
issues.evidence: GET /api/extras/cameras?incident=2024-horse-gulch-889237 -> unavailable, state_not_available, sources ['caloes_webcams','alertcalifornia','caltrans_cctv']. docs/screenshots/review3-us-official-cameras-nonca-desktop.png, bottom of the cameras panel.
issues.fix: In cameras_payload, return sources [] for state_not_available (as evacuations does), or have CameraPanel hide the source list for that reason code. Extend test_cameras_outside_california.

issues.problem: In a mixed CA/OR answer (Brookings), Cal OES's 'none listed' caveat keeps its brief-2 text, which names no source: 'No orders or warnings are listed here right now. That is not an all-clear…'. Next to it is 'Oregon OEM lists no evacuation zone here right now…'. A reader cannot tell which state the first sentence covers.
issues.fix: Keep the brief-2 sentence for California-only answers, which must stay identical. When more than one source answered, prefix it with the state ('California: …') or use the per-source form ('Cal OES lists no evacuation zone here right now…'). Add a test on the Brookings mock.

The report records this as a deviation, and model.test.ts covers the California-only answer.
